issues.legal_issue: An award cannot be remitted for stamping under the power to remit an award for reconsideration when the absence of a stamp is a defect outside the award and no reconsideration of its merits is sought.
material_facts: An arbitration agreement was filed in court and the court referred the dispute to an arbitrator.
The arbitrator made and filed an award, which was unstamped.
The court remitted the award to the arbitrator to have it rewritten on stamped paper and resubmitted; the direction was not for reconsideration of the merits.
issues.conclusion: The award could not be remitted for stamping under the statutory power to remit an award for reconsideration.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 16(1)(c) of the Arbitration Act, 1940, an award may be remitted where an objection to its legality is apparent on its face. That concerns an error of law in the award itself or in a document incorporated into it on which the arbitrator based the award, and permits reconsideration of the merits; it does not encompass a defect dehors the award, such as want of stamp. The Court approved Nani Bala Saha v. Ram Gopal Saha, AIR 1945 Cal. 19, and disapproved Ramkumar v. Kushalchand, AIR 1928 Nag. 166, and Lakshmichand v. Kalloolal, 1956 N.L.J. 504.

rule.if: court_referred_arbitration and award_made_and_filed and award_unstamped and court_remitted_only_for_stamping

predicates.court_referred_arbitration: A court referred a dispute to an arbitrator under an arbitration agreement.
predicates.award_made_and_filed: The arbitrator made an award and filed it in court.
predicates.award_unstamped: The award lacked a stamp required for it.
predicates.court_remitted_only_for_stamping: The court directed the arbitrator to rewrite or resubmit the award only to address its lack of a stamp, not to reconsider its merits.

issues.definition: When a court-referred arbitration has produced a filed, unstamped award and the court remits it only for stamping, the remittal is not permitted.

issues.legal_issue: A court cannot use its inherent procedural power to direct an arbitrator to make a fresh award after the arbitrator has made the award and become functus officio.
material_facts: The arbitrator had already made and filed the award when the court directed the arbitrator to prepare and resubmit it on stamped paper.
The direction required the arbitrator to act again after making the award.
issues.conclusion: The court's inherent power did not authorize it to direct the arbitrator to make a fresh award or resubmit a stamped copy.
issues.legal_principle: Section 41 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, made the Code of Civil Procedure applicable to court proceedings under the Act, but section 151 of the Code could not authorize an order contrary to the established principle that an arbitrator is functus officio after making an award. The Court relied on Mordue v. Palmer, (1870) L.R. 6 Ch. App. 22, for the principle that an arbitrator who has signed an award cannot of his own authority remedy it. A further copy would not be the award on which action could be taken.

predicates.arbitration_court_proceeding: A court was dealing with a proceeding arising from an arbitration.
predicates.award_already_made: The arbitrator had already made the award before the court gave its direction.
predicates.court_directed_arbitrator_to_make_fresh_: The court directed the arbitrator to prepare or submit a new version of the award after making the original award.

issues.definition: In an arbitration court proceeding, once the arbitrator has made the award, a court direction to prepare a fresh award cannot be authorized by inherent power.

issues.legal_issue: The powers to correct clerical mistakes or accidental slips and to modify or correct an award do not authorize directing an arbitrator to rewrite an unstamped award and resubmit it.
material_facts: The court directed the arbitrator to rewrite the award on stamped paper and resubmit it.
The direction was not made as a correction of a clerical mistake or accidental slip, and the court did not purport to modify or correct the award.
issues.conclusion: The direction to rewrite and resubmit the award could not be supported by the statutory powers to correct clerical mistakes or accidental slips or to modify or correct an award.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(d) of the Arbitration Act, 1940, concerns correction of clerical mistakes or accidental slips; omission to stamp an award is neither. Section 13 is enabling and does not permit the arbitrator to be compelled to exercise its powers. Sections 15(b) and 15(c), which concern a court's power to modify or correct an award, did not provide a basis for the order made.

predicates.arbitration_award_proceeding: A court was dealing with an award made in an arbitration proceeding.
predicates.award_unstamped: The award lacked a stamp required for it.
predicates.court_ordered_rewriting_for_stamping: The court directed the award to be rewritten to address its lack of a stamp.

issues.definition: When an unstamped arbitration award is to be rewritten for stamping, the powers to correct or modify an award do not authorize that direction.
